writeup: TIC 238618726 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.1667 days. The primary eclipse causes the star to dim by 11.82 percent, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 374.2 in automated TESS photometry. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 45.1 and a centroid offset of 1.9 arcseconds. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be a previously unknown system. The automated screening model assigned it a score of 0.40 on its likelihood scale. All data quality checks passed without flags, though this result relies solely on automated analysis from TESS observations.
